entries.title: Tour replaced by a recorded tour window
entries.text: The site tour now plays as a recorded tour window with 33 steps, replacing the live tour that ran on the real pages. Earlier the same day it was reworked from Daniel's notes (smoother scrolling, cold-start fixes). Live since 2026-10-22.

entries.text: The Whose position box in the case reader now appears only when the Development tab's Experimental setting is on. It is hidden by default. Live since 2026-10-22.

entries.title: Judge issue outcomes hidden
entries.text: The judge profile and the two-judge comparison no longer show outcomes by issue, and the outdated wording about them is gone. The other judge figures are unchanged. Live since 2026-10-22.

entries.title: Tour rewritten step by step; long tour removed
entries.text: The tour now has 30 steps with one card per step, the extra Short tour buttons are gone, and the long tour is removed. A follow-up fix keeps the hover step from being hidden by the corner card on a first visit. Live since 2026-10-21.

entries.title: Short tour reworked
entries.text: The short site tour was reworked from feedback: it now highlights whole regions of the page and gives each side tab its own step. Live since 2026-10-21.

entries.title: Case reader: new header card and wider citation cards
entries.text: The case reader has a header card at the top, an About tab, a two-line Authorities list and wider citation cards. Desktop only for now; phone width still needs follow-up work. Live since 2026-10-21.

entries.title: New About page title page, overview and diagrams
entries.text: The About page opens with a new title page, a clearer overview and diagrams of how the library fits together. Live since 2026-10-21.

entries.title: Faster result counts and ranking
entries.text: The result counts down the side are worked out from one list of matching cases instead of several, and ranking reads each case's details once. Results are the same, only faster. Live since 2026-10-21 (deployed that morning, no database change).

entries.title: Searches that run too long are stopped
entries.text: Every search now stops after 20 seconds. A very broad word such as "Canada" now shows a "too broad" message instead of hanging. Live since 2026-10-20.

entries.title: A short tour of the site
entries.text: A short site tour now sits beside the existing Take a tour button, for a quick look at search, the case reader and judges.

entries.title: Judge clean-up tools; link clean-up applied
entries.text: Tools to delete junk judge profiles, merge duplicate names and remove repeated judge links were merged. On 2026-10-20, 14,605 repeated Federal Court and Federal Court of Appeal judge links were removed from the live database, and 45 junk judge profiles (with their 385 links) were deleted, both with a backup and an undo file. The site code is live. Some junk names remain in Federal Court and Federal Court of Appeal judge lists.

entries.title: Stricter citation links
entries.text: New links made from a case name or title are now checked against the court and date. Live since 2026-10-20. Existing wrong links stay until a separate script to unlink them is run; it is merged but has not been run.

entries.title: French decisions read correctly (code live, stored decisions not yet corrected)
entries.text: The reader for French-language decisions now finds the judge, file number and outcome more reliably for decisions read from now on. The code is live since 2026-10-20. Decisions already stored are corrected by a separate script that has not been run yet.

entries.title: Faster search
entries.text: Broad searches find case numbers first and then load details, there is a date index, and a broad word shows one result per case. Live since 2026-10-20 (database index added the same day).

entries.title: Argument lists (off by default)
entries.text: A first reader of the main arguments on each side, with a rule for choosing which to keep. The code is live since 2026-10-20 but switched off, so it has no effect on the site until turned on.

entries.title: Judges: fewer junk names, better counts
entries.text: Lines such as counsel labels are no longer mistaken for judges. Judge court chips and two result counts were corrected. Decisions that are not immigration cases are left out of judge win rates.

entries.title: Repair scripts for self-citations, own-caption links and junk judges
entries.text: Reversible clean-up scripts were added for wrong self-citations, own-caption links and junk judge names. They were applied to the live database on 2026-10-20 with a backup and undo files, so the live data was corrected.

entries.title: Experimental pages explain themselves
entries.text: Experimental landing pages say what they are, the site has a proper not-found page, and it has a browser tab icon.

entries.title: Statute pages open the real case reader
entries.text: Decisions listed on a statute page now link to the full reader.

entries.title: Search: year filter, topic words and full-text search
entries.text: The year filter now matches the year counts shown beside it. Short topic searches also match the tags stored on each case. Full-text search no longer takes up to a minute. Impossible values in the year, sort or paging boxes now give a clear message.

entries.title: Faster start and lighter data calls
entries.text: The home page loads tabs only when you open them, and asks for less data on startup. Long lists of citing cases and the library inventory are returned in pages.

entries.title: Clear error messages instead of crashes
entries.text: Odd characters in a search or a case number that does not exist now give a plain error instead of a server crash page.

entries.title: A case's own citations are left out of its authorities
entries.text: When a decision cites itself, the citation is no longer counted among the authorities it relies on.

entries.title: Case reader: tidier header, Back button and activity links
entries.text: The facts in the case header now wrap instead of being cut off, including on a phone. Back leaves the case and returns to your results. Federal Court activity links show only for immigration files.

entries.text: A gold set and evaluator measure how many statute references are found (the baseline was 64.7 percent recall). Extraction now handles provisions of any Act, decimals and lists, CBSA acts, Federal Courts Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection Rules and bare “Rule N”, with guards against wrong anchoring, and refugee decisions tie “the Act” and sections 96 to 98 to the IRPA. The stored references are still being repaired.

entries.title: Hover shows the paragraph or provision cited
entries.text: Hovering a pinpointed citation shows the text of the paragraph it points to, and hovering a statute reference shows the stored provision text. Pinpoints written as ranges, lists, “ff” and several paragraphs per citation are now read correctly. Conventions and treaties now appear as statutes rather than as unmatched citations.

entries.title: Citation extraction: reject weak short forms and title-block name-only rows
Case type filter (labels not stored yet)
entries.text: Search can filter by what kind of case a decision is, with counts. It only shows options once the case-type labels are stored in the library, which has not happened yet.

entries.title: Case types: rule-based “what kind of case is this”
entries.text: Fixed rules label each decision as, for example, a judicial review of an immigration decision, using the text header, the IMM docket number and the subject named in the opening, with no AI. Unclear decisions are resolved from the subject in the opening, immigration-party decisions are kept out of the “not immigration” group, and rows can be exported for review. A dry run is checked before anything is stored; the labels are not stored in the library yet. The reader gains a case-type chip once they are.

entries.title: Citation extraction: French, parentheses and landmark short forms
entries.text: French citations, parenthesised citations and bare landmark short forms such as “Vavilov at para N” are now linked. A new side-by-side writer stores refined results next to the originals instead of overwriting. A scanner that took minutes on long judgments was fixed, and a decision’s own docket numbers are no longer read as citations.

entries.title: Statute importer fixed and statute library pages
entries.text: The importer no longer drops sections past the first hundred and reads section numbers correctly. The Statute Library page shows the sections of each Act with case counts, text and the decisions that cite them, and a dry-run backfill fills provision columns from pinpoints.

entries.title: Filter by the case a decision cites, and by tag
entries.text: Advanced search can now require that results cite a chosen case, and can filter by legal tag.

entries.title: Judge names cleaned up, step by step
entries.text: A judge-name normalizer and a read-only report came first, then a reversible way to merge duplicate profiles, Federal Court docket activity on each judge profile, Supreme Court panels split into individual judges, court-specific rules for the Federal Court of Appeal and Supreme Court, and every Federal Court of Appeal bench member linked rather than only the author. Stale or wrong merges were pruned. The rules are not yet applied to the stored data.

entries.title: Case fingerprints (draft)
entries.text: A draft way to find similar decisions by subject and shared authorities. It is not connected to the site.

entries.title: Case search redesigned
entries.text: A new search page with a floating search bar, an Advanced filter panel, boxed result rows, Recent cases and a Show more button. Polish followed: relevance sort, an RPD court chip and a cleaner Minister list.

entries.title: Clean case information in the reader
entries.text: The header shows court and citation, the case name, then the file number, decision date and decision maker (“Justice Mosley”), with the outcome and source links. The About panel lists the same facts in a fixed order, and a bug that left Authorities text stuck on “Loading” was fixed.

entries.title: Case structure: a role for each paragraph
entries.text: Discussion-unit boundaries were improved and pruned, and each paragraph can be labelled with its role in the decision (such as issue or analysis) by rules, with no AI. These labels sit behind “Show experimental”.

entries.title: About page rewritten for the demo
entries.text: The About page was rewritten to describe the demo as it stands on 6 October: what is live, what is coming soon and what is still in progress, with the funding section removed. The Changelog was brought up to date.

entries.title: Formatted reader redesigned
entries.text: A left panel, a title card, click cards for citations and authorities, search inside the decision, a slim one-row header and a reader that fills the screen height.

entries.title: Four sections along the top: About, Case search, Intelligence, Coming soon
entries.text: The site now opens on a short, clear set of sections. Judge Profiles, Citation Intelligence and Federal Court Analytics sit under Intelligence / Statistics, and every other feature has its own page under Coming soon with a short explainer and a banner saying it is not finished. Nothing was removed; the pages still open by direct link.

entries.title: Markup mode and Live Analysis paused as “Coming soon”
entries.text: Markup is greyed out in the reader’s view switcher under a Coming soon strip and cannot be opened, and Live Analysis is paused the same way. The code is untouched. Before the pause, Live Analysis could open your own memo, factum or decision in Markup, link “above” and “Ibid” back-references (marked as a guess), and had its library lookup fixed.

entries.title: Scheduled intake: first foundation
entries.text: The first piece of an automatic intake of new decisions was written. It only discovers what is new (a dry run) and is not running.

entries.title: Results explain themselves
entries.text: Each result shows a highlighted excerpt of why it matched, court and year chips to narrow in one click, a sort bar, a Copy citation button, and a plain-words line under the search box saying what the search is doing.

entries.title: Unfinished reader tools hidden behind “Show experimental”
entries.text: The summary cards, case-structure and paragraph-assessment tools, Similar paragraphs and the legal-development notice no longer appear by default, so the reader shows only what is ready. The Testing tab and Core cases tools are behind the same switch.

entries.title: Markup mode: Acts layer and closer fidelity
entries.text: Markup gained a layer for statutes with provision text, header pills for outcome, judge and file number, shorter margin labels and richer citation cards. Hover cards and Peek panels now show the pinpoint paragraph’s text and an “In this case” line, and every highlighted citation responds to hover and click.

entries.title: Faster search and faster case opening
entries.text: Filter counts load lazily, full-text search uses an index, citation counts load after the results appear, and a decision opens faster because its data is located once per case.

entries.title: Rule-based citation treatment and cited-by upkeep
entries.text: An experimental rule-based endpoint reads how a citing decision treats an authority, and the paragraph cited-by data is kept current in small bounded steps beside the live site.

entries.title: User text stays away from models
entries.text: Anything typed or uploaded is kept away from AI models unless enhanced AI mode has been switched on, and the opt-in research chat provider can point at a local or other compatible model. Search itself stays free of AI.

entries.title: Accessibility fixes
entries.text: Two accessibility errors found by an automated check were fixed.

entries.title: Judge Profile compare form tidied
entries.text: The two-judge comparison form and two search-page links were tidied.

entries.title: Tag Analytics tab fixed
entries.text: The Tag Analytics tab never opened and its data call failed. Both are fixed, and it is listed under Coming soon.

entries.title: Extractive case summary card
entries.text: A summary card built only from sentences in the decision, each linked to its paragraph, for quick triage. It is behind “Show experimental”.

entries.title: Precedent finder, memo gap suggestions and stored-data comparison
entries.text: Describe a legal issue and get the authorities cited by decisions with matching tags, with explained rankings; a memo check can suggest authorities it is missing; and two decisions can be compared side by side from stored data only. All are listed under Coming soon.

entries.title: Friendlier when the database is down
entries.text: If the database is unavailable the pages show a plain message and each panel can retry on its own. Requests now carry IDs, slow requests are logged, and optional database timeouts and limits on heavy endpoints protect the site.

entries.title: About page refreshed and Changelog added
entries.text: The About overview was audited against the code, and a Changelog view was added with this timeline built from GitHub history.

entries.title: Margin shows who cites each paragraph
entries.text: A batch job records which cases cite each paragraph and the signal beside the citation (followed, distinguished, quoted). The margin uses it once it has been run on the live data.

entries.title: Markup mode: Word export and private notes
entries.text: Export the decision with its margin notes as real Word comments. Click a paragraph number to write a private note or highlight; these stay in your browser only and travel into the Word file.

entries.title: Docket number column made safe to add
entries.text: A database change to the docket number column was written so it can be applied repeatedly without harm.

entries.title: Phone layout fixes
entries.text: Search, the reader and Markup mode now fit narrow screens: stacked search fields, scrolling filter chips, a one-row Markup toolbar and bottom-sheet panels. A second pass fixed Site Architecture, wide tables, judge comparison and the statute viewer.

entries.title: Markup mode: hover card, Peek panel, topic view
entries.text: Hover a citation for a quick look, open floating Peek panels without leaving the case, show tags as tint or bubbles, and group the text by topic.

entries.title: Fixed script errors that could break pages
entries.text: Several syntax errors in the page scripts were fixed.

entries.title: Markup mode: a third way to read a case
entries.text: The decision fills the page with notes in the margin: citations, discussion units, outcome, judge and who cites each paragraph. A switcher turns each layer off or on, case information sits in a drawer, and an outline and Find tool help navigate.

entries.title: Outcomes now say “unclear” instead of guessing
entries.text: Fixed wrong outcome patterns found in an accuracy audit. When the rules cannot tell, the case now shows as unclear. A second-opinion checker tool can only confirm an outcome or mark it unclear, and writes its answers separately from the main data.

entries.title: Groundwork for a local AI model
entries.text: Optional building blocks for running AI on a local machine: switchable embedding providers, versioned prompts, and tools to compare models offline. All are off by default.

entries.title: Search stays free of AI by default
entries.text: Searching through the API no longer sends the query to an outside AI service unless that mode is switched on. The Case Search page itself already ran on the database alone.

entries.title: Easier to host and monitor
entries.text: Docker setup, health probes, a separate background job runner, a smaller set of required packages and automated dependency checks make the site easier to move and run elsewhere.

entries.title: Documentation refreshed for readiness
entries.text: The README and architecture overview were refreshed and an evidence-backed set of government-readiness documents was added.

entries.title: Opt-in sign-in, audit log and safety limits
entries.text: A password gate and a privacy-safe request log exist but are off by default. Uploads are size-limited and extra security headers are available. Access stays open for now.

entries.title: Quick summary in the reader
entries.text: A short summary built only from sentences in the decision itself, shown in the reader sidebar.

entries.title: See how courts have considered a statute section
entries.text: For a section of a law, a view of the decisions that have considered it.

entries.title: Cautious overruling-risk notice
entries.text: A yellow note appears on a decision when an authority it relies on may have been affected by later case law, with the source and reasoning shown. It draws on an editable list meant for lawyer review.

entries.title: Memo check suggests missing and contrary authorities
entries.text: After a memo is checked, the tool can suggest authorities that similar cases cite which the memo does not, and some that point the other way.

entries.title: Unit search and judge analytics
entries.text: Search discovered legal themes and see how different judges handle them.

entries.title: Statute library with point-in-time versions
entries.text: Federal laws relevant to immigration and CBSA work (22 of them) can be imported with their history, so a decision links to the version of a section in force on its date. A statute viewer page and API were added.

entries.title: Importer for a larger public case-law dataset
entries.text: A tool to bring decisions from the public A2AJ dataset into the library, with a check that skips cases already held. Dry runs and diagnostics come first.

entries.title: Saved-search digests
entries.text: Digests of what is new on a saved search, with a flag when the Minister lost and a note when a trend shifts.

entries.title: Power-user search operators
entries.text: Quoted phrases, exclusions and field operators for people who want exact control.

entries.title: Judge comparison and issue outcomes
entries.text: Compare two judges side by side by issue. Outcome shares always show how many decisions were left out, and unclear results are counted rather than hidden.

entries.title: Side-by-side case comparison
entries.text: Open two decisions next to each other to compare what they decided and cited.

entries.title: Reader keyboard shortcuts and printing
entries.text: Move between paragraphs with the keyboard and print a decision cleanly.

entries.title: Faster analytics pages
entries.text: Slow analytics endpoints now keep their results for a short time instead of recalculating on every visit. Database indexes to speed up search were drafted.

entries.title: Word export of search results
entries.text: Download search results as a Word document next to the CSV option.

entries.title: Exact citations and party names match first
entries.text: Typing a neutral citation or a party name now puts that case at the top of the results.

entries.title: Explainable paragraph similarity
entries.text: Find similar paragraphs and see which shared tags and citations make them similar.

entries.title: Most-cited paragraphs panel
entries.text: A collapsible panel lists the five paragraphs of a decision that the most other cases cite.

entries.title: Printable legal issue briefs
entries.text: A printable page for a legal issue with yearly outcomes, courts and the key authorities. Outcome percentages show how many cases were unclassified.

entries.title: Saved searches and alerts return
entries.text: Saved searches and alerts were rebuilt inside the redesigned case search.

entries.title: Case search exports to CSV
entries.text: Download the current search results as a spreadsheet.

entries.title: Readiness and review documents
entries.text: Written checks of privacy and security for the document tools, an accessibility audit, a documentation fact-check against the code, a readiness checklist for government use, performance findings, and designs for ID and IAD decision coverage and for citation-treatment signals.

entries.title: Theme Discovery groups sub-themes
entries.text: Related sub-themes in the Legal Themes tab are grouped by shared key terms.

entries.title: Discussion units and outline navigator
entries.text: Decisions are split into discussion units with an outline you can jump around, plus a Citation Context pane showing which sub-topic cites a linked case.

entries.title: Tag-based case finder and tag ranking
entries.text: Find cases similar to the one you are reading by the legal tags they share, and see the most distinctive tags first.

entries.title: Analyst quick-start guide
entries.text: A plain guide to using the tool, written for litigation analysts.

entries.title: Extractive summary in the reader
entries.text: A summary made only of sentences taken directly from the decision, each linked back to its paragraph.

entries.title: Paragraphs shaded when other cases cite them
entries.text: The reader shades paragraphs that other cases in the library have cited.

entries.title: Tagging improved and widened
entries.text: Detention grounds and decision-maker actions are now tagged, country-name false positives were fixed, and the tag set grew to 323 common legal concepts, about 3.6 times the earlier coverage.

entries.title: Memo citation check
entries.text: Upload a Word or PDF memo and see the cases and statute sections in it matched and linked to the library. It works in memory and saves nothing.

entries.title: Better outcome detection
entries.text: The rules that decide whether a decision allowed or dismissed an application were improved.

entries.title: Citation Intelligence and Judge Profiles redesigned
entries.text: Both pages were rebuilt with clearer layouts and faster navigation from a case to its authorities and from a judge to their decisions.

entries.title: Federal Court activity expansion and FC Analytics tab
entries.text: Many more docket outcomes are read, including consent settlements. Judges at each stage, hearings, appeals, stays of removal, counsel and deadlines appear in the data, and a new FC Analytics tab shows interactive charts over it.

entries.title: Second-pass checks on citations and statutes
entries.text: Extra refinement layers re-check each case citation and statute reference for correctness.

entries.title: De-identify tool
entries.text: A page that finds names in a document and swaps them for placeholders, then restores them, all in memory with nothing stored.

entries.title: Case search redesigned
entries.text: Quick filters, new result cards and a cited-by count on every result. The unused RAG option was removed.

entries.title: Reader sidebar, header and context pane redesigned
entries.text: A new reader layout with a case summary sidebar, a clearer header and toolbar, and a context pane for linked cases.

entries.title: Citations highlighted inline in the reader
entries.text: Citations sit inside their paragraphs as flat highlights, and clicking a linked case in the reader works as expected.

entries.title: The site now runs as a background service
entries.text: The site and its secure tunnel start themselves when the computer logs in, run out of sight, and restart if they stop. Tests also began running automatically on every proposed change.

entries.title: New formatted case reader
entries.text: Decisions now open in a clean formatted view with headings, numbered paragraphs, block quotes and signatures set properly, made by fixed rules rather than AI. It became the default way to read a case.

entries.title: Ingestion and embedding workflow improvements
entries.text: Updates to how new decisions are brought in and indexed, ahead of the site moving to its own always-on service.

entries.title: About page rewritten as a status overview
entries.text: The About page was restructured into a plain status overview with site architecture on its own tab. A Research Bench prototype tab for saving decisions and notes was added.

entries.title: Project time and cost records
entries.text: Records of recorded work time and spending were refreshed and added to the project’s documentation.

entries.title: Federal Court files tracked by stage
entries.text: Docket reading now knows which steps apply at each stage of a file, so a file refused leave is no longer shown as missing a hearing. Motion types were classified and linked to the docket entries they came from, and the decision being challenged is identified for a sample of files.

entries.title: Paragraph meaning linked to citations
entries.text: Paragraphs in the core decisions were linked to the citations inside them, and the About page gained a per-case pipeline diagram.

entries.title: Interactive map of how the site works
entries.text: The About page gained a clickable map showing how decisions flow from source to research tools. Site architecture details moved to their own tab.

entries.title: Discussion units on a core set of decisions
entries.text: A resumable run began splitting decisions into discussion units (stretches of reasoning on one issue) for a core set of 300 decisions.

entries.title: Case search made clearer
entries.text: The search page was reorganised for clarity and a more compact chunk view was added to the reader.

entries.title: Case summary layer
entries.text: A switchable summary built by fixed rules from what is stored, with no AI involved.

entries.title: Case information and advanced views split
entries.text: The reader’s side area separates basic case information from the advanced layers, and a new evidence layer shows how the decision’s own statute and case references line up.

entries.title: Reader fixes: highlights, keyboard and speed
entries.text: The decision reader now loads statute references only when needed, highlights overlapping citations and laws more clearly, and can be used from the keyboard. A visual accessibility review was recorded.

entries.title: Citation extraction rebuilt and checked
entries.text: The citation reader was hardened and re-run across the library, with a recorded checkpoint of how many citations were found and linked.

entries.title: Supreme Court decisions brought in from 1970 on
entries.text: A resumable run read Supreme Court of Canada decisions (text only) from 1970 forward, with safeguards that set aside any decision that stalls.

entries.title: Second-generation legal tagging goes live
entries.text: A larger, evidence-based set of legal-topic tags replaced the first one, with each tag tied to the text that triggered it.

entries.title: Legal Themes tab
entries.text: A tab for exploring which legal themes and statute sections show up across decisions and how they cluster.

entries.title: Foundation for statute authority linking
entries.text: The groundwork for tying each statute reference to the real provision it names was laid, along with a plan for what to build next.

entries.title: Composite citations and pinpoint accuracy
entries.text: Citations written together, such as a case with attached pinpoints, are now read as one unit. Pinpoint reading was improved and tested against a hand-checked five-case sample.

entries.title: Tags highlighted where they occur
entries.text: Legal-topic tags can now be shown at the exact place in the decision where they are found, and a watchdog keeps long tagging runs on track.

entries.title: Live analysis and wider citation matching
entries.text: A live analysis page that works on text you give it without saving anything, and a much broader pass at matching short-form citations to the right case.

entries.title: Laws and regulations linked to the cases that cite them
entries.text: A reference system for legislation was added, so citations to sections of the Act and Regulations connect to the provisions themselves.

entries.title: Federal Court docket entries get classified
entries.text: Rules were added to recognise what each docket line means (filing, leave decision, hearing, judgment) and to review samples by hand.

entries.title: Docket numbers and the Federal Court activity layer
entries.text: Cases gained a docket number (filled in for nearly all of them), and a separate layer began holding the day-by-day docket of Federal Court immigration files.

entries.title: Case search matches titles and citations first
entries.text: Searching now looks at case names and citations by default, and only reads the full text when you ask it to, which is faster and less noisy.

entries.title: One tabbed research page
entries.text: Search, Citation Intelligence, Judge Profile and the other tools were brought together on one page with tabs. Judge and citation sub-tab searches were fixed.

entries.title: Citation Intelligence page and the first About page
entries.text: Pick a case and see who cites it, when, and how. The site also got a shared header and an About page that showed live library counts.

entries.title: Data Explorer: advanced filters
entries.text: The main research page gained filters for court, year, judge, outcome and Minister, with several sort modes. A large pass linked citations to the cases they name inside the library.

entries.title: Pinpoints and “paragraph 34(1)(f) of IRPA” forms recognised
entries.text: Citations now keep their pinpoint (for example, “at para 99”). Statute references written in different orders, such as “34(1)(f) of IRPA”, are all recognised.

entries.title: Citation Pass QA page
entries.text: A review page that compares the citations and statute references the system stored against what it finds live in the text, colour-coded, so mistakes are easy to spot.

entries.title: Decisions split into sections and paragraphs
entries.text: Every decision is now divided by headings and numbered paragraphs, so a result can point to the exact passage. Federal Court details such as judge and dates got confidence checks.

entries.title: Citation analytics: shifts, gaps and bridges
entries.text: Early analysis of how authorities are used: which doctrines are shifting, which cases are cited together, and which authorities a decision does not mention that similar decisions do. The first stand-alone case reader and a citation map arrived too.

entries.title: Federal Court decisions brought in directly
entries.text: Federal Court decisions can be collected from their source with the original page address and details preserved.

entries.title: Overnight processing that can stop and resume
entries.text: Large batches of decisions can now be processed overnight, stopped, and picked up again where they left off, with a lock so two runs never collide. A first legal-topic tag list and a separate library of statutes and guidance were added.

entries.title: First version of the case library
entries.text: A database of Canadian court decisions that could be searched by keyword and by meaning, with the original text kept untouched alongside what was read from it.
